docs(architecture): how-flyway-works — sequence diagrams, state machines, contracts

Versioned architecture walkthrough showing how flyway works concretely:

- §1 Mental model (substance / surface / transport)
- §2 Component diagram — packages × on-disk artifacts × agent runtimes
- §3 What works today (with real sequence diagrams):
  - Skill installation (ADR-0006 mechanism)
  - flyway_init via CLI
  - flyway_init via MCP (stateless — artifacts return to agent)
- §4 Cross-murmuration consent (conceptual; surface defined, execution
  pending) — full negotiation arc from tension → signed agreement
- §5 State machines: Identity, Tension, Proposal stages, Agreement
- §6 Contracts: the 9 tools, the agreement schema, entity statement
  shape, DID document shape, the seven protocol invariants

Mermaid diagrams render natively on GitHub. Linked from README.
Tied to SHA eec423c so future revisions can refresh against changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(core+cli+mcp): flyway_init — first tool that actually runs

The first crossing from "specification" to "system." flyway_init now
generates real artifacts:

- A did:web DID derived from a GitHub repo URL
  (did:web:github.com:owner:repo)
- A W3C-compliant DID document with a JsonWebKey2020 verification
  method (ed25519 public key in JWK form)
- An entity statement carrying Source metadata (name, mode, supported
  tools, supported schemas, verification key reference)
- A real ed25519 keypair generated via Node's built-in crypto.
  Private key in PKCS#8 PEM with mode 0o600.

Architecture per the surface/substance separation we've kept consistent:

- packages/core/src/init.ts — pure functions (parseRepoUrl, deriveDid,
  generateEd25519Keypair, buildDidDocument, buildEntityStatement,
  flywayInit). No file I/O. 19 tests.
- packages/cli/src/init.ts — wraps flywayInit + writes files to the
  canonical paths per research paper §6.7:
    .well-known/did.json
    flyway/entity-statement.json
    flyway/keys/source.key
  Ensures .gitignore excludes flyway/keys/. Refuses to overwrite
  without --force (private key loss is unrecoverable). 9 tests.
- packages/cli/src/bin/flyway.ts — adds `flyway init --repo-url ...
  --source-name ... [--mode interactive] [--force]` subcommand.
- packages/mcp/src/handlers.ts — flyway_init now actually runs (calls
  flywayInit, returns the artifacts to the agent). Other tools still
  return "not yet implemented." The MCP handler is stateless — the
  agent (or CLI) writes the files. Updated handler tests: 3 cases for
  flyway_init (valid input → artifacts; missing args → isError;
  invalid URL → isError); existing "not yet implemented" test
  preserved for other tools.

End-to-end smoke test confirms CLI and MCP both produce the same DID
and matching artifacts for the same input. 85/85 tests passing across
7 test files.

Signing of the entity statement is the next layer (uses the private
key we now generate). That, plus implementations of the remaining 8
tools, are the work that follows.

README updated to reflect that "tool execution is unimplemented" is
no longer true — flyway_init runs.

chore: install flyway skill into the flyway repo itself (.claude/skills/flyway/)

Eating our own dog food. Any Claude Code session opened against the
flyway repo now loads the flyway skill automatically, giving the agent
the full S3-grounded consent vocabulary when reasoning about flyway
operations on flyway itself.

Installed via the ADR-0006 mechanism we just shipped:
  node packages/cli/dist/bin/flyway.js skill install flyway

Note: this file is generated from FLYWAY_SKILL_MD in
@murmurations-ai/flyway-agent. When the protocol instructions or tool
definitions change, re-run the install command to refresh. (Drift
detection — a CI test asserting this file matches the registry — is a
future quality-of-life addition.)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(cli): implement ADR-0006 — flyway skill list / install / uninstall

flyway-cli stops being a stub. Three subcommands ship in v0.1:

- flyway skill list                       — show available and installed skills
- flyway skill install <name> [--target P] — write SKILL.md folder to target
- flyway skill uninstall <name> [--target P] — remove the skill folder

Target resolution per ADR-0006: .claude/skills/ if .claude/ exists in
cwd; otherwise ./skills/. Explicit --target always wins. Re-installing
warns when local content differs from the registry version.

Architecture per ADR-0006:
- packages/cli/src/skill.ts holds the registry + the four operations
  (list, install, uninstall, inferTarget). Pure functions, testable
  without a transport.
- The CLI imports FLYWAY_SKILL_MD from @murmurations-ai/flyway-agent
  via workspace dep; never hardcodes skill content. Adding a future
  skill means publishing a package and registering it here.
- bin/flyway.ts does argv parsing + dispatch with plain Node — no
  CLI framework dependency, matching the small-protocol principle.

Tests: 15 new (registry shape, list with installed/modified/absent
states, install behaviour incl. nested target creation and tampering
warning, uninstall idempotency, target inference for .claude/ and
default). 55/55 total passing.

End-to-end smoke test confirms all subcommands work against a real
temp directory, target inference switches correctly when .claude/
appears, and tampering produces the expected warning.

This closes retrospective gap #6: skills move from "exported constants"
to "installable artifacts." flyway-cli row in the README updated from
"Stub" to "Wired."
